title.narrative: World Bank's Umbrella Trust Fund on Jobs, phase 2 (2020-2024)
World Bank's Umbrella Trust Fund on Jobs, phase 2 (2020-2024)

description.narrative:
Insatsen innebär ett fortsatt stöd till Världsbankens paraplyfond för jobb om 80 MSEK, för fas 2 (2020-2024). Detta är en fortsättning på stödet till fas 1 (2015-2020) som uppgick till 54 MSEK.
Fondens övergripande mål är att:
a) stötta utformning och implementering av omfattande, integrerade och högeffektiva jobbstrategier på landnivå
b) främja global kunskap om effektiva policyer och interventioner för hållbart jobbskapande, särskilt för de mest utsatta grupperna
Detta uppnås genom tre fönster med fokus på:
1) Skala upp sysselsättnings-ansatsen i Bankens operativa verksamhet på landnivå
2) Förbättrade uppföljnings- och resultatmätningsmetoder
3) Globalt kunskapande genom partnerskap och innovation
Bankens målsättning är att samla totalt motsvarande ca 469,3 MSEK för fondens andra fas.

The contribution constitutes a continued support to the second phase of the World Bank's Multi Donor Trust Fund (MDTF) for Jobs (2020-2024) of 80 MSEK. This is a continuation of the support to the fist phase (2015-2020) which was 54 MSEK.
The objectives of the Fund are:
a) To support the design and implementation of comprehensive, integrated and high-impact jobs strategies for WBG client countries
b) To advance global knowledge on the most effective policies and activities for sustainable jobs, especially for the most vulnerable groups
The work is organised through three windows:
Window 1 - Supporting Jobs Lending at Scale
Window 2 - Measurement Agenda
Window 3 - Global knowledge production through External Partnerships and Innovation
The aim for the second phase is to raise a total of equivalent to 469,3 MSEK.

The World Bank Multi Donor Trust Fund (MDTF) for Jobs was established in 2014 as one of the first Umbrella Trust Funds within the World Bank Group, and the second phase runs from 2020-2024.
The second phase of the MDFT Jobs maintains the original objectives of the Fund:
a) To support the design and implementation of comprehensive, integrated and high-impact jobs strategies for WBG client countries
b) To advance global knowledge on the most effective policies and activities for sustainable jobs, especially for the most vulnerable groups
This is achieved through the following 3 windows:
Window 1 - Supporting Jobs Lending at Scale: This window provides technical expertise resources to task teams in other GPs and IFC to help scale up the WBGs jobs lending portfolio across sectors and regions, in order to improve technical quality of operations for improved targeting jobs outcomes and scale up operational approaches especially in low-income and fragile settings.
Window 2 - Measurement Agenda: This window advances the technical capacity for measurement of jobs outcome, and upgrades country level data and diagnostics on jobs outcomes, to enable evidence-based jobs initiativs and provide policymakers with improved information on expected impact of interventions.
Window 3 - Influence through External Partnerships and Innovation: Under this window, the Jobs Group support a strong engagement and dissemination and outreach between the World Bank Jobs Group and other key stakeholders, to identify and accelerate cutting edge solutions to emerging jobs challenges.
The goal for the second phase is to ramp up the emphasis specifically on country level operationalization, as well as the measurement of outcomes, and the work with governments, private sector actors and development partners to reinforce the agenda of private sector-led jobs growth.
The overall theory of change is that the MDTF provides direct technical support to country level operations with job-centric designs to enhance jobs outcomes in programmes, provide measurement methodologies, and engage with private and public partners for effective solutions, to increase capacity for implementation of effective programmes and policies in countries and across sectors supported by evidence and data, to ultimately contribute to the accelerated creation of better jobs through scaled up public sector reforms and private sector investments.

The World Bank is one of the leading global actors in the area of job creation. The Jobs and Growth Unit contribute to both global knowledge production as well as strenghtening the institutional capacity for country operations to develop and implement strategies, policies and programmes for more and better jobs for people living in poverty.
Under President Bangas leadership the World Bank Group has placed job creation at the center of its development agenda, recognizing it as essential to tackling poverty and addressing the looming employment crisis. To deliver on this ambition, the World Bank launched a three-pillar jobs strategy and established a High-Level Jobs Council to scale employment in five priority sectors. Institutionally, the WBG is mainstreaming the jobs agenda and building systems to track impact through a new Corporate Scorecard and jobs indicator methodology.
In this period, the Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund (MDTF) made significant contributions to advancing the World Bank Groups jobs agenda through development of diagnostics, data systems, analytical tools and country level operations. The work done under the MDTF Jobs both enabled the current acceleration of the jobs agenda that Banga is driving as well as paved the way for it. Without the work under the Fund the Presidents jobs agenda would not have been able to expand as significantly as it has.
Strengthening institutional capacity at country level
During the last year, the MDTF supported the development and rollout of the new Country Growth and Jobs Report (CGJR) at country level, a core diagnostic tool that places jobs at the center of country-level analysis and strategy. This includes the creation of key tools including the Quick Jobs Scan, data harmonization methods, and standardized guidelines now integrated into CGJR methodology and piloted in countries such as Bangladesh and Cameroon. These outputs are directly informing policy dialogue and shaping future Country Partnership Frameworks.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 16, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1] [NAT/INST]
The MDTF Jobs also supported improved labour market data and analysis in for example Nigeria where the national survery instrument was enhanced with migration data to advance the understanding of climate-induced mobility, labour informality and gender employment dynamics. The new models were also shared with teams working in Morocco, Tunisia, Djibouti and Burundi for potential adoption.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 17, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1] [NAT/INST]
In Ghana the MDTF Jobs conducted work to better understand the significance of gender role attitudes on employment outcomes. The results of the study, showing that gender role attitudes and personality traits are significant factors shaping labour maket participation and employment choices, provide a base of evidence for the government to act in appropriate ways, for example through providing more accessible and affordable childcare programs as well as removing barriers to business registration.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 18-19, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1, M2] [NAT/INST]
MDTF Jobs also assisted government partner to develop policies around digital labor market platforms, to improve labor market outcomes in low and middle-income countries. For example, a study was conducted on the emerging public-private partnership models for effective delivery of labor intermediation services in Ghana, and a pilot aimed to provide high-quality evidence on the labor market dynamics of platform work in Brazil was conducted with the aim to contribute to how these should be regulated.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 24-25, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1] [NAT/INST]
The MDTF grant supported a feasibility study on greening jobs in waste collection and tourism in Lao PDR. The grant activities focused on addressing knowledge gaps in the waste and recycling and Nature Based Tourism (NBT) sectors in Lao PDR and to identify opportunities to support inclusive job growth and the introduction of innovative technologies in waste management. This grant supported the institutional capacity building of the central government of Laos and local government in Vientiane; and the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 28-29, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1] [NAT/INST]
Global knowledge products
Examples of global knowledge products supported during the year is the completed analytical work and draft of the Jobs for Development Report (J4D). The report focuses on two core areas: (i) empirical insights into the drivers of more and better jobs, and (ii) a policy framework to help countries craft job strategies focused on Production, People, and Places. Despite the delay in publication, the insights generated by the analytical work performed for the J4D Report have significantly contributed to shaping the new jobs agenda set forth by President Banga. Particularly with regards to the emphasis on the quality aspect of jobs (better jobs) as well as on the interdependence between jobs outcomes and a countrys growth dynamics.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 19, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1] [GLOB/NORM]
Another global product is addressing the knowledge gap on the impacts of the green transition through innovations in both data and methodologies. It aims to produce policy-relevant evidence on climate change risks to the poor and vulnerable and on how to protect them from welfare losses and benefit from the low carbon transition.
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 31, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1] [GLOB/NORM]
The MDTF Jobs also supported a number of knowledge products on the back of the previously published and well received "Working without Borders: The Promise and Perils of Online Gig Work":
- A short note focused on local/regional digital gig platforms and their role in supporting labour market inclusion
- A short note on gender gaps on digital gig platforms
- A short note on digital jobs for poor, vulnerable and low skilled workers
(Source: Jobs Umbrella Multi-Donor Trust Fund Annual Report 2024, s. 21, DOX: 20/001323-112) [M1, M2] [GLOB/NORM]
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
